label: late original-phase token after q/g (weak, diffuse conjunction)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.0056% of steps). About 92% of mass is in the late original phase (t=4..8, mostly 0-2 tokens before <DEL>, longer sequences L=8-9), with weak spillover onto <DEL> and the first copy steps. It is enriched when the previous token (or the one before) is q or g, when the sequence starts with v/d/c, and when the current token is m/t/2/r/a/o, but each cue only gives 3-14x lift and no conjunction gets precision above about 15%. The best simple predicate (late original phase with prev token q/g) covers about half the mass at 0.2% precision. Magnitude is fairly flat (mean 0.13, max 0.225) and none of these cues clearly modulates it. Never fires at t<4 and almost never during the middle of the copy phase. This looks like a sparse conjunction of several history cues that a simple predicate cannot capture.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=v (+3.77), orig2=m (+2.95), prev_tok=q (+2.73), orig2=a (+2.48), orig0=d (+2.40), prev_tok=g (+2.37). Lower it: in_tok=g (-2.59), prev3_tok=- (-2.57), orig_idx=-1 (-2.12), t=3 (-2.02).
